note: What the driver reads to tell a failure of the INFRASTRUCTURE under `claude -p` from a role's own result (design/driver.md, FR-13: closed variety lives in data, code reads it). `scripts/infra_failure.py` is the reader. `failures[]` is tried in file order against the result text plus stderr, and only when the call failed (`is_error` or a non-zero exit) - the text of a successful call is never matched (FR-12). A row is `{id, kind, pattern, reset_pattern?, retry_code?, evidence}`: `kind` is `auth` (the person must sign in), `limit` (the account's usage limit is reached; `reset_pattern`'s first group is quoted to the person verbatim) or `transient` (the same call is tried again by `runtime_policy.retry_decision(retry_code, ...)`, and a row with no `retry_code` is never retried). Patterns are Python regexes with no flags argument: a row that wants one carries it as a leading `(?i)`. A row whose pattern does not compile is skipped with a printed note, the others still match. `not_infra_subtypes[]` are result subtypes of `claude -p` that are the role's own outcome even though `is_error` is true (`error_max_turns`: the role ran out of turns, which the repair path already handles). A failure no row matches is `unclassified` and reaches the callers exactly as before. A row whose `evidence` says `unmeasured` was written from the service's documented behaviour and has not been seen on the wire yet: measure it before trusting its wording. `child_env` is what `claude -p` children lose from the driver's own environment: a driver started from a desktop-app terminal inherits the host's proxy address without the per-process token, so every child answers `Not logged in` while a valid login sits in the credentials file. `remove` names variables, `remove_prefixes` removes every variable that starts with one of them, `remove_named_by` names variables whose VALUE is the name of one more variable to remove. A project brings its own gateway or API-key setup through `driver.child_env.keep` in qa-factory/config.json (kept even when listed here) and adds names with `driver.child_env.remove`. Rows named `codex_*` are the same vocabulary for the Codex CLI (`story_run.py --host codex`): a `turn.failed` or `error` event of `codex exec --json` puts its message into the result text, and these rows read it; every one is `unmeasured` until a run records the wording. A row may carry `hosts` (a list of host names): it is tried only for a call of one of those hosts, a row without the key for every call, and a caller that names no host tries the rows without the key only (the `codex_*` rows carry `["codex"]`, so a role's own text on Claude never reads as a Codex login failure). `default_model` is the model a host runs when `--model` is not given, by host (CX1-15, the owner's word 20.10.2026: `codex` runs the latest Terra); `claude` is not listed, its default is `sonnet` in the driver. The Codex host with no `--model` and no `default_model.codex` here stops with a refusal naming this key.
